assumptions: Ordinary integral homology of a connected oriented cyclic CW graph with N=m*L vertices and edges; N=2 is a two-edge CW circle, not an abstract simplicial complex.
The generator of C_m sends vertex/edge v to v+k*L modulo N, 0<=k<m; no edge reversals.
The normalized group-bar complex tensored with cellular chains models ordinary homotopy-orbit chains. The chain computation through degree2 is sufficient only for H1.
A group-fixed point is stronger than trivial action on H1. No A1-localization or Nisnevich-sheaf comparison is assumed.
Universal topological and motivic bridges require independent review; no parent solution or novelty claimed.
target: Test whether the fixed-basepoint hypothesis can be dropped from the ordinary H1 Borel-quotient splitting for cyclic rotations of a circle; distinguish a homotopy quotient from the coarse quotient.
